newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Deng's health stable, children take holiday - report.
newsitem.headline: Deng's health stable, children take holiday - report.

text.p: China's ailing patriach Deng Xiaoping is in relatively stable health and his children were confident enough to leave him at home to enjoy the sun on a remote tropical island, a Hong Kong newspaper said on Tuesday.
The independent daily Ming Pao quoted sources from Beijing as saying Deng's son and daughters would not have left for Hainan Island in southern China if his health was unstable.
Deng's eldest son Deng Pufang and his wife and daughters Deng Lin and Deng Rong, had left Beijing for Hainan at the start of this month, Ming Pao quoted the source as saying.
It said they would return to Beijing before the Chinese Lunar New Year festival, which falls on February 7.

Deng has not been seen in public since early 1994. In his last appearance he looked frail and faltering. Speculation abounds about his health, ranging from rumours he was admitted to hospital in recent days to reports he remains at home with little change in his health but with his lucidity failing.
